evidence.observation: The public queue class under contract. It owns a `Map<string, SerialQueue>` keyed by asset id, so every distinct source key gets its own single lane; `enqueue` reuses that lane and `onIdle` is the drain barrier used to observe completion. Because a source is addressed by a stable key (the code_graph_id / wiki_id), all submissions for the same source are funnelled onto the same SerialQueue, which is what makes duplicate submissions serialize instead of racing.

`enqueue(key, job)` looks the key up in `this.queues` and only constructs a new `SerialQueue` on a miss (`if (!q) { q = new SerialQueue(key); this.queues.set(key, q); }`), then hands the job to that lane and returns immediately (fire-and-forget with the rejection swallowed because the job already persisted its own failed status). Consequence for the contract: two `enqueue` calls with the same key never create two workers — the second is appended to the first's lane and can only start after the first drains.

`onIdle(key?)` awaits a specific lane's `onIdle()` or `Promise.all` over every lane. This is the deterministic synchronization point the fixture uses to prove the double-submission run has fully drained before reading the final status, so the recorded terminal state is not a race-dependent snapshot.

The lane implementation BuildQueue delegates to. `add` pushes a FIFO entry and calls `drain`, which (lines 81-101) runs at most one task at a time and re-drains only after the running task settles. This enforces concurrency=1 per key, the mechanism that makes a duplicate same-source submission run strictly after the first rather than concurrently.

The service entry point exercised by the fixture. It calls `store.createCodeGraph(params)` and only calls `this.enqueueBuild(row)` when the store reports `!existed`. A second submission of the same source returns `existed: true`, so no second job is enqueued and no second effective build is produced — the idempotency half of the contract.

The re-trigger path returns `{ kind: "busy", ... }` without changing status or enqueuing a job when the asset is still `pending`/`processing`. The fixture calls `sync` while the first build is in flight and observes `busy`, proving a duplicate in-flight submission is rejected rather than queued alongside the running build.

The dedup primitive behind `create`: it selects an existing non-deleted row by `(service_id, team_id, repo_url, branch)` and returns `{ existed: true }` on a hit, only inserting a freshly generated `cg-` id on a miss (with unique-violation races also resolving to the existing row). The in-memory stub in the fixture mirrors exactly this source-keyed idempotency so the demo reproduces the production decision without better-sqlite3/drizzle installed.

claims.claim: BuildQueue assigns each source key exactly one SerialQueue and reuses that lane for every enqueue, so duplicate submissions of the same source are serialized on a single lane and can never rebuild concurrently; the fixture confirms this with same-key max concurrency = 1 and FIFO event order start:a1, end:a1, start:a2, end:a2, while two distinct keys still overlap (max concurrency = 2).

Submitting the same source twice produces exactly one effective build: the first create inserts the row and enqueues one job, and the second create is deduped at the store by (service_id, team_id, repo_url, branch) returning existed=true so no second job is enqueued. The fixture observes effective_builds = 1, persisted_rows = 1, second_submission_existed = true.

A duplicate submission that arrives while the source is still pending/processing is rejected as busy by sync without enqueuing, so the in-flight build is not doubled; the fixture records concurrent_resync = busy.

The queue records the expected terminal state: after BuildQueue.onIdle drains the single lane, the asset status is ready, with the status transitions pending -> processing (cloning) -> processing (indexing) -> ready and no failed state. The fixture asserts terminal_state = ready and internal stages cloning -> indexing -> cleared.

conclusion: Contract holds. Driving the real CodeGraphService on top of the real BuildQueue, with only the persistence seam stubbed in memory, a source submitted twice yields one effective build (one worker invocation, one persisted row) and settles in the expected terminal state ready. The same-source path is guarded at three levels: the store dedups create() by (service_id, team_id, repo_url, branch) so the second submission never enqueues; sync() rejects an in-flight duplicate as busy; and BuildQueue keys each source to a single SerialQueue lane, so even if duplicate work reached the queue it would run strictly after the first build rather than concurrently. The executable fixture emits 12/12 passing checks.
